verdict.rationale: Gumloop's docs describe a webhook trigger that gives an agent its own unique URL. Any external caller that can send an HTTP POST (Stripe, GitHub, scripts) starts an agent run, and no API key or SDK is needed. The data sent to the URL is described as firing the trigger, so the core of inbound webhook-triggered runs is covered. Missing for 10: detail on how the payload is parsed and mapped into the run, webhook authentication or signature verification, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can expose a custom webhook URL that receives external HTTP requests and starts a workflow run with the payload

citations.quote: A webhook trigger gives an agent its own URL. Anything that can send an HTTP POST — Stripe, GitHub, a cron job, an internal script — runs the agent by calling it.
a webhook trigger to fire when another app sends data to a unique URL.
Webhooks, covered next, let an outside service run an agent by calling a URL — no API key, SDK, or polling loop needed.
